difficultyRationale: Tests the conflict-resolution rule when a class inherits unrelated default methods with the same signature.
prompt: A class implements two unrelated interfaces, and both interfaces declare a default method with the same signature. Neither default is more specific. What must the class do to compile?
explanation: When unrelated inherited defaults conflict and no rule selects one as more specific, the implementing class must provide an overriding method that resolves the conflict.

options.text: Nothing; Java chooses the first interface listed in implements.
options.explanation: The order of interfaces in the implements clause does not resolve a default-method conflict.

options.text: Override the method and resolve the conflict explicitly.
options.explanation: An overriding declaration in the class removes the ambiguity.
Final prevents subclassing but does not resolve inherited default methods.
That would change the interfaces themselves; it is not the rule for resolving inherited defaults in the class.

references.title: JLS 9.4.1.3 Inheriting Methods with Override-Equivalent Signatures
